findings.finding: BETA has beaten the TOP of its own quarterly revenue guide on both 2026 prints (Q1 $10.13m vs $7-10m guide; Q2 $14.66m vs $8-11m, 33% over the top end, driven by EPFD and Florida DOT charger deliveries); Q3 is guided $8-12m with consensus $10.77m, so a repeat of the pattern implies ~$12-14m, i.e. ~+10-30% vs consensus - but this stock fell -2.58% and -3.29% on the last two beats, the second with a FY revenue raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 revenue beat top of guide: -2.58% (2026-05-12). Q2 2026 beat top of guide by 33% and raised FY revenue guide to $42-50m: -3.29% (2026-08-12). Beats have been sold on both occasions.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $10.77m sits at the guide midpoint rather than above the top end where the last two prints landed, so the sell side has not extrapolated the beat pattern; if it had, the Q3 revenue estimate range would centre on $13-15m rather than top out at $12.3m. Small because revenue is ~$45m/yr against a ~$4.8bn market cap and is not the line the stock trades on.
findings.independence: Q1 beat vs $7-10m guide from a separate document: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1913786/beta-technologies-q1-earnings-call-highlights ; Q3 guide $8-12m from the Q2 call transcript https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/12/beta-beta-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ . Same company, same disclosure stream.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 (Aviation Week, NBAA) CEO Kyle Clark said CX300 certification is 'taking longer than he initially expected' and listed 'motor certification' among goals for 'the year ahead' - the H500A engine, guided to FAA type certification in H1 2026 and described in July as 'closing in', is still uncertified - while 2027 revenue consensus is $361.65m (vs ~$47m for 2026), a ramp that requires CX300 certification and deliveries; the Q3 release/call is the first formal venue to restate (likely push out) certification timing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The H1 2026 H500A target slipped at the Q1 print (2026-05-12, -2.58%, together with an EBITDA guide cut); price targets were cut by Citi ($33->$25), BTIG ($40->$33) and Cantor ($38->$31) around that time citing revised delivery expectations. No print yet has carried a dated CX300 slip.
findings.why_not_priced: The remark was made in a trade-press interview the same week as the A250 market-survey authorization, and the stock rose 6.1% that week; sell-side kept Buy ratings and $31-35 targets (Needham reiterated $34 on 10-21, Barclays initiated $35 on 10-09) and the 2027 revenue consensus still sits at $362m. If the slip were priced, 2027 estimates and targets would have been cut. Partly priced: the stock is -44% from its high and the put skew is +6.6 points, so this is sized well below the implied move.
findings.independence: Q2 call (12 Aug) already flagged 'execution risk left on the H500A' with no date given: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/12/beta-beta-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ ; original H1 2026 target and Q1 slip: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1913786/beta-technologies-q1-earnings-call-highlights . No document yet gives a new date.

findings.finding: The EXIM financing expansion of up to $1bn net ($830m incremental, non-dilutive) announced 2026-08-04 was only an 'intent', subject to due diligence and definitive documentation, and no press release or 8-K since (EDGAR shows no 8-K after August) reports it closing; a closing or a firm timeline announced with Q3 would remove the dilution overhang on a company burning ~$400-445m adj. EBITDA plus $150-200m capex a year against $1.48bn cash.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Announcement of intent on 2026-08-04 was not a print; no print-day history on financing.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether it closes is unknown; the stock is -44% off its high with a rising short base (7.8m -> 14.6m shares Aug-Oct), consistent with the market discounting a future equity raise. The money funds a manufacturing ramp corroborated by a $3.9bn / 1,001-aircraft backlog, so a closing is a positive; a further delay is a small negative. Sized small because nothing says it closes this week.
findings.independence: Q2 call: talks ongoing, 'it will materially extend our financial runway', no timing given (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/12/beta-beta-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). findings.finding: FAA granted BETA a Special Airworthiness Certificate for market surveys on the ALIA A250 eVTOL (announced 2026-10-21, first such authorization for an eVTOL; first flight Plattsburgh-Burlington 20 Oct), and BETA completed 14 all-electric flights in Florida under eIPP (release 2026-10-30) - milestones the Q3 release will restate as the quarter's highlights.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stock rose 6.1% on 2026-10-21 on the authorization (MarketBeat item per search); not a print-day item.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the 5-day run-up of +4.4% is this news. Residual is only that the release can frame it as A250 progress ahead of the CTOL certification update. The authorization is explicitly not type certification.
findings.independence: https://investors.beta.team/news-events/press-releases (lists 10-21 and 10-30 releases); https://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/safety-ops-regulation/beta-details-vtol-progress-following-faa-market-survey (same event, shares the 10-22 interview with finding 2).

findings.why_not_priced: Visible on EDGAR and pre-scheduled; essentially priced and immaterial in size (~$200k/day against ~$30m/day turnover).

findings.finding: Short interest nearly doubled into the print, from 7.8m shares (3.3% of float, 2026-08-20) to 14.59m shares at 8.0 days to cover (2026-10-15), roughly 12% of a ~117.6m Class A float, while put/call open interest is 0.4 - a growing short base that a better-than-feared certification update or EXIM closing would have to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with this short base; short interest was ~3-5% of float at the August print (-3.29%).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the bet the market has made, not information it lacks; a squeeze is a mechanism only if the release is not as bad as the shorts expect. 8 days to cover makes a positive surprise move faster than a negative one.

baseline_tension: The one material negative (certification slipping, not yet dated) agrees with the +6.6 vol-point put skew and the -44% drawdown, so it is probably partly priced; against it sit a near-doubled short base (~12% of float, 8 days to cover) and a beat-the-top revenue pattern that this stock has nonetheless sold twice, so the evidence nets to roughly zero with a slight negative lean.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; beats sold twice): revenue-beat finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, and print_vs_bar trimmed from +16% to +12% because the Q2 overshoot was partly one-off charger deliveries.
Lesson 7 (positioning): certification-slip negative agrees with the +6.6 put skew (likely priced) and sits on ~12% of float short at 8 DTC - cut from -2.0 to -1.5; p_up moved from 46 to 47.
Lesson 5 (inference/thin bar): EPS-revision finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1 because only two analysts carry EPS and the sources disagree.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): EXIM finding kept positive at +0.3 after checking the money funds a ramp corroborated by a $3.9bn backlog.
Lesson 6 (bar and window): bar sourced to company guide plus three agreeing estimate sources; Joby read-across kept in outside_window; nothing else changed.
